newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares close slightly higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares close slightly higher in slow trade.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange made slight gains Tuesday, led mostly by a rise in the Brazilian and other regional stock markets, brokers said.
Analysts said it was difficult to give a clear prediction for Wednesday but added that the bolsa might rise due to expected good first half financial reports of companies.
According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index rose 0.34 percent to 2,104.42 points, while the blue-chip selective index also rose 1.64 percent to 3007.36 points.
The total amount traded was 43.6 million soles ($16.5 million) in 2,439 transactions. Overall, 37 shares went up, 32 dropped and 28 remained stable.
"I believe that the regional rise was a technical rebound, caused by the recuperation of the Brazilian bolsa," said analyst Manuel Torres from Finvest brokerage.
Analysts said the market was further waiting for the presidential Independece Day address on July 28, hoping it would restore investor confidence following the recent political instability.

But Mariano Prado from MGS y Asociados brokerage said the market regained confidence following last week's political turmoil and Torres said investors were in fact not expecting much from the presidential message.
Regional concerns were expected to continue affecting the bolsa.
"(Investors) are more prudent with the Lima bolsa in face of the situation in Brazil and New York," said Prado.
The Brazilian bolsa had rocketed 7.07 percent and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) was up 1.74 percent by 1910 GMT.
The NYSE rose sharply following an upbeat report to Congress by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
Market leader telecommunications giant Telefonica del Peru rose 1.61 percent to 6.30 soles.
"The regional rise pushed Peruvian ADRs, especially those of Telefonica del Peru who was knocked down in recent days," said Torres.
Other winners included brewer Cervecera Backus y Johnston with 3.07 percent to 2.35 soles, miner Morococha with 4.9 percent to 7.50 soles and electrical Luz del Sur with 0.32 percent to 3.09 soles.
Losers were electrical Edegel with 0.91 percent to 1.09 soles and Edelnor with 5.0 percent to 1.90 soles and miner Minsur with 5.2 percent to 8.20 soles.
Financial company Credicorp, which trades ADRs in New York, also closed higher at $19.75 with a 2.81 percent rise.
